** Should a vendor excluded before a weekend stay excluded when its market reopens?
   :PROPERTIES:
   :ID:       F-M-9
   :KIND:     brief
   :COMMAND:  resolve
   :OPTIONS:  accept_risk,repair
   :ACCEPT_OPTION: accept_risk
   :REFUSE_OPTION: repair
   :QUESTION: Should a vendor excluded before a weekend stay excluded when its market reopens?
   :RECORD_VERSION: 1
   :CANDIDATE_SHA:  c0ffee15d0000000000000000000000000000000
   :CONTRACT_VERSION: 4
   :CONTRACT_SHA256:  a1b2c3d4
   :RUN_ID:   05661870
   :PHASE_ID: atlas-15d
   :END:
   Today: Pyth's NVDA product reopens Sunday 20:00 ET[2]. Right now the excluded vendor rejoins at the first tick at or after that reopen, even though its first quote after a long break is often stale.
   Impact: No market stops publishing[2]. At most one vendor is missing for about 10 s after a weekend reopen, so the published price is formed from one vendor fewer for that window[3].
   Options:
   - Keep as is [accept_risk] — the vendor rejoins immediately at the first tick after the reopen[3] Cost: one stale first quote can enter the price for up to 10 s[3]
   - Hold it out [repair] (recommended) — the vendor stays excluded until 10 s after the reopen, then rejoins[4] Cost: 10 s with one vendor fewer at a reopen[4]
   Recommendation: Hold it out — IC §5's re-entry rule asks for a settled first tick, not the first tick after a break
   Related:
   - [[*Should the re-entry band be ten seconds wide?][D-A-80 — Should the re-entry band be ten seconds wide?]]
   - [[file:messages/T-54.org][T-54 — Should every held market make no offer at all until a vendor returns?]]
   Glossary: [[file:glossary.org::Owner glossary][window]]
   Evidence (original):
   - [1] message: F-M-9 a vendor excluded before the weekend rejoins immediately at the first tick after a reopen
   - [2] config: calendars.yaml us_equity opens Sun 20:00
   - [3] code: src/core/blend.rs:88 the re-entry test reads the band only
   - [4] code: src/core/blend.rs:41 the band constant is read here

** Should the re-entry band be ten seconds wide?
   :PROPERTIES:
   :ID:       D-A-80
   :KIND:     brief
   :COMMAND:  resolve
   :OPTIONS:  accept_as_implemented,reject_and_repair
   :ACCEPT_OPTION: accept_as_implemented
   :REFUSE_OPTION: reject_and_repair
   :QUESTION: Should the re-entry band be ten seconds wide?
   :RECORD_VERSION: 2
   :CANDIDATE_SHA:  c0ffee15d0000000000000000000000000000000
   :CONTRACT_VERSION: 4
   :CONTRACT_SHA256:  a1b2c3d4
   :RUN_ID:   05661870
   :PHASE_ID: atlas-15d
   :END:
   Today: Stork's BTCUSD product trades around the clock: its 24/7 calendar runs every minute of 00:00 to 23:59[2], so it has no reopen. The band now uses 10 s[3], the value the decision chose, and the excluded vendor rejoins when a fresh tick lands inside it.
   Impact: No market stops publishing[2]. The wider band lets one more vendor back in after a quiet spell, so the price is formed from more vendors more of the time[3].
   Options:
   - Accept it as implemented [accept_as_implemented] (recommended) — 10 s stays the re-entry band[3] Cost: a genuinely stale vendor can rejoin after 10 s[3]
   - Reject and repair [reject_and_repair] — a new attempt picks the band again, with a further allowance Cost: a further repair round; no market stops publishing either way
   Recommendation: Accept it as implemented — the panel's own count of re-entries agrees with IC §5's 10 s[3]
   Glossary: [[file:glossary.org::Owner glossary][band]]
   Evidence (original):
   - [1] message: D-A-80 widen the re-entry band to 10 s failed its vote
   - [2] config: calendars.yaml crypto_24_7 rth 00:00-23:59
   - [3] code: src/core/blend.rs:41 the band constant is read here

** Should the last good price be published while a market is held?
   :PROPERTIES:
   :ID:       D-B-82
   :KIND:     brief
   :COMMAND:  resolve
   :OPTIONS:  accept_as_implemented,reject_and_repair
   :ACCEPT_OPTION: accept_as_implemented
   :REFUSE_OPTION: reject_and_repair
   :QUESTION: Should the last good price be published while a market is held?
   :RECORD_VERSION: 1
   :CANDIDATE_SHA:  c0ffee15d0000000000000000000000000000000
   :CONTRACT_VERSION: 4
   :CONTRACT_SHA256:  a1b2c3d4
   :RUN_ID:   05661870
   :PHASE_ID: atlas-15d
   :END:
   Today: Kaiko's XAUUSD product closes Friday 17:00 ET for the weekend[2]. The current candidate does not publish during that held window; when the market reopens Sunday 18:00 ET[2] the first fresh price is published.
   Impact: No market stops publishing[2]. While XAUUSD is held there is simply no offer, which is the documented behaviour; the change only affects whether the last price is repeated[3].
   Options:
   - Accept it as implemented [accept_as_implemented] (recommended) — no offer is published while the market is held Cost: consumers see no update for the held window
   - Reject and repair [reject_and_repair] — a new attempt makes the held market repeat its last good price Cost: a further repair round; a stale price can be mistaken for a live one
   Recommendation: Accept it as implemented — IC §7 says a held market makes no offer, and a repeated price would read as live
   Related:
   - [[file:messages/T-54.org][T-54 — Should every held market make no offer at all until a vendor returns?]]
   Glossary: [[file:glossary.org::Owner glossary][window]] [[file:glossary.org::Owner glossary][held]]
